Emotion regulation interventions influenced the emotional behavior, emotional experience, autonomic physiology, and interpersonal behavior of both the manipulated and non-manipulated partners in a relationship conflict.

the suppression of emotions during relationship conflict increased cardiovascular arousal and negative emotion among both the manipulated person, and among the partner of the manipulated person, whereas the induction of a positive mindset during relationship conflict decreased cardiovascular arousal and positive emotion among both the partner of the person who was instructed to adopt the positive mindset and among the partner's partner.

emotion regulation interventions (affective suppression and positive mindset induction) influenced the physiology, behavior, and emotional experiences of the manipulated person and the partner in the relationship conflict interaction, and that the effects were moderated by attachment orientations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how individuals and their partners regulate their emotions during relationship conflicts.
how people manage their emotions in the context of conflict interactions with romantic partners.
the interpersonal regulation of emotions during relationship conflict interactions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

emotion regulation interventions influence the physiology, emotional experience and emotional behavior of both the manipulated and the non-manipulated person, and the effect is moderated by attachment orientation.
emotion regulation strategies are not always effective, and that their effectiveness is contingent on the emotional context and the attachment style of the person who is using them.
the way in which we manage our emotional experience and expression during conflict is a key factor in the success and failure of our relationships.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of emotion regulation interventions are bidirectional and that the impact of such interventions depends on attachment orientations.
the way in which one regulates his or her own emotions during a conflict interaction can affect the way in which the other partner experiences the interaction.
